atoms.text: British colonialism developed into two main forms: settler colonialism and extractive colonialism.
atoms.sound: British colonialism developed into two main forms: settler colonialism and extractive colonialism.

atoms.text: Settler colonialism involved large-scale European migration. Settlers established societies similar to those in Europe, often displacing indigenous populations and limiting their political power. These colonies, with strong white settler populations, often gained independence earlier because White people were considered capable of self-rule.

instruction.text: Where did the settlers come from?

atoms.a: European settlers integrated into indigenous culture.
Colonies with European settler majority gained independence earlier.

atoms.text: On the other hand, extractive colonialism focused on the exploitation of resources and people. Colonised regions were used to produce raw materials and crops for the British Empire. Local and enslaved populations formed the majority and were forced into labour, while British colonists remained a small ruling minority in administrative and military roles.

atoms.a: Extractive colonies were exploited for British profit and industry.
British colonists were forced into labour.

atoms.text: Colonisation disrupted existing political and economic systems. However, it was not uncontested. British control often began with treaties and indirect influence, followed by military intervention when resistance occurred, eventually leading to full colonial rule.

b: British colonialism is characterised by immediate takeover.
